title.narrative: Rapid Emergency Deployment Initiative (REDI): Emergency Funding and Enhancement of Preparedness, Response, and Safety Security of First Responders and Local Actors Along Frontline Territories

description.narrative: ltpgtThe recent escalations in Kharkiv Oblast highlighted the urgent need to develop more adaptive and streamlined approaches to funding for local responders, one that is aligned with their proven ability to rapidly mobilize and address emergencies. NP seeks to address this through Rapid Emergency Deployment Initiative (REDI). Through proactively equipping local actors with appropriate and proportional equipment, coupled with deployment of emergency funds, REDI will bolster a local actor network both capable and well positioned of responding to emergencies in real time. REDI will identify local actors and coordination bodies, the specific contingencies or emergencies they are best positioned to respond to and rapidly activate partner response projects when needed. This will be realized through planning and preparedness to preapprove all required paperwork, which has proven to be a key limitation to emergency response. REDI will provide necessary “seed funds” necessary to have local mechanisms ready and withhold a proportion of requested funds in anticipation of partner project implementation and deploy resources as needed to the ever-changing context. Should a given contingency not emerge, these funds and project can then be extended or later reallocated to highest priorities. This approach is in itself an Early-Warning-Early-Response mechanism, aspiring to find balance between preparedness and planning with rapid response.ltbrgtFurther, through the provision of a sub-grant and additional support directed towards Relief Coordination Center (RCC), this project will reinforce current preparedness for local response mechanisms, ensuring they are well-trained, well-equipped and thus well-prepared to handle emergencies effectively. This component of the project will be directed to sustain and expand the scope of RCC’s existing volunteer Public Development Center (PDC). Focused on strengthening and sharing volunteer experience and skills. The PDC is physically in Kharkiv, thus, the project will support access to volunteers in Donestska through provision of transportation support for volunteer network staff in the Oblast. NP, RCC, and partner networks will ensure that volunteers are prepared to handle emergencies in a way that supports civilian and volunteer safety, encompassing Do-No-Harm principles, and protection safeguards. By harmonizing such policies, the project will support a coordinated and standardized approach to emergency response, enhancing the overall effectiveness, accountability, and impact of local efforts. ltbrgtFurthering the impact and scope of volunteer safety and preparedness, REDI aims to establish an armored vehicle evacuation group, through the Safe Transport for Evacuation and Emergency Logistics (STEEL) initiative, co-developed with RCC. STEEL is comprised of specialized, trained, and experienced volunteers/staff from multiple local NGOs and volunteer networks across NP program sites. This group will conduct civilian evacuations in hard-to-reach and frontline areas, utilizing armored vehicles, personal protective equipment (PPE), and communication equipment to minimize the risks of injury and loss of life. Through AVs, REDI seeks to enhance safety backstops for evacuating civilians and the volunteers who facilitate these critical operations. NP and RCC will promote volunteer collectives to have continued and strong communication with CIMIC and regional administration, ensuring that they are aware of movement prior to deployment and that the right permits and access have been granted. By equipping this specialized evacuation group with the necessary resources and training, this project will significantly bolster the capacity and safety of local responders to operate in high-risk environments, ensuring the safe extraction of civilians from conflict zones.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
